In 1971, once his brother and he himself went to the said food godown for giving lunch to his father and found many people there. They were loading food grain from the godown into a truck. After some times, a jeep reached there and 3/4 persons got down from the jeep and saw the occurrence of loading of food grains from the godown in the truck. Sometimes thereafter, Pakistani army and the some people rushed there giving "Pakistan Zindabad" slogan. Hearing such slogans, the people present there fled away. Those persons and Pak army entered into food godown. The appellant was previously not known to him but his brother Mostafa disclosed the name of the appellant to him. Pakistani army and appellant and his

 

bahini abased the officers and staffs of food godown with filthy language. Thereafter, keeping some Pakistani army for the security of the godown, they left the godown. Few days thereafter; this witness and his brOther again went to that food godown and found that the officers and staffs had been kept confined in a room of the Dukbangalow. After Johor prayer, they found that the victims were brought near the bank of river of Khoai. This witness and his brother saw that occurrence hiding themselves in a sugarcane field. He saw that the appellant Qaiser gave signal and then members of the Pakistani army shot those victims who died in the spot instantly. The assailants threw the dead bodies of those 7(seven) unfortunate victims including the father of this witness in the river. In cross examination, he denied the defence suggestion that the statements made above are not true.

 

284. P.W.12 Gour Prosad Roy, who was a student leader of Brindabon College, Habigonj in 1971. In his testimony, he stated that on 29th May, 1971 at about 4.00 p.m. he .found the appellant Qaiser standing near the approach road of the bridge of river Khoai. He also found 7(seven) officers and staffs of the food godown in standing condition near the bank of river Khoai. He saw that the appellant Qaiser gave a signal by his hand indicating the members of Pakistani army who shot those the 7(seven) victims, consequently, they died on the spot. Thereafter, they threw their bodies in the river of Khoai. He stated that he had been able to identify victims Abdul Aziz, Sub-divisional food controller, Chief inspector Abdul Khaleque, O.C. L.S.D. Razaul Karim guard Geda Miah, Abdur Rahman and Mazed Ali and carrying contractor Tara Miah. In his cross examination, he denied the defence suggestion that he did not see the occurrence dated 29.05.1971.

 

285. Mr. S.M. Shahjahan, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that the statements of the witnesses, namely, P.W.9, 11 and 12 are contradictory and discriminatory and they are the planted witnesses, the Tribunal committed error of law in believing the testimonies of those witnesses.

 

286. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney General appearing for the respondent, submits that P.Ws.9, 11 and 12 were the eye witnesses of the occurrence of killing 7(seven) unfortunate unarmed civilians who were the officers and staffs of Shaestaganj food godown, the Tribunal rightly believed the testimonies of those eye witnesses and convicted the appellant.

 

287. We have gone through of evidence of P.W.1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12. It is not disputed that the Sub-divisional Food controller Abdul Aziz, Chief Inspector Abdul Khaleque, Officer in Charge of food godown Rezaul Karim, guard Abdur Rahman, Geda Miah, Mazed Ali and handling contractor Taia Miah were killed on 29.05.1971 near Railway bridge of river Khdai. Out of those 7 witnesses, P.W.8, 9, 4, 11 and 12 were the eye witnesses of the occurrence. P.W. 9 and 11 specifically said at the time of confining of those Unfortunate victims they were present at food godown of Shaestaganj Bazar. P.W.9 and 11, sons of victim Mazed Ali, followed the killing of squad and saw that the victims were kept confined in a room of Shaestagonj Dukbangalow. P.Ws.9 and 11 also saw that the appellant was talking with the Pakistani army in the field of Dukbangalow and thereafter, they pressurized the victims to go to the bank of river Khoai near railway bridge. P.Ws. 9, 11 and 12 also saw that the appellant Syed Qaiser gave signal to kill the victims and, pursuant to that signal, Pakistani army shot the victims who receiving bullet injuries died on the spot. Thereafter, the dead bodies were thrown in the river Khoai. At the time of giving descriptions of confinement and killing of their father, P.Ws. 9 and 11 started crying in the witness box of the tribunal and identified the appellant. P.W. 9 specifically stated that his father nursed the appellant during his childhood but he did not bother to kill their father. P.W.12 Gour Prosad Roy himself saw the occurrence of killing of those 7(seven) unarmed civilians at the instance of the appellant on the date of occurrence dated 29.05.1971. We do not find any contradictions and discrepancies in the testimonies of P.Ws.9, 11 and 12. The shooting of those 7 unarmed civilians were carried out in accordance with the instructions of the appellant. He played active part in the killing of those unarmed civilians purely on his personal motive. The Tribunal did not commit any error of law and facts in believing the testimonies of those 3(three) witnesses and convicting the appellant. The afore-said crimes committed and indulged in by the appellant were gruesome, cold blooded, heinous and cruel. Considering the consistent evidence of P.Ws.9, 11 and 12, we are of the view that the Tribunal did not commit any error in awarding the capital sentence of the appellant Qaiser Ali for commission of the offence as stated in the charge No.5. Charge No. 6.

 

288. "On 29th April 1971; at any time after 03:30-04:00 pm at a place of 'Duran Bazaar' point at Shaestaganj, [under the then Habiganj sub-division) accused Syed-Md. Qaiser asked the members of Pakistani armed force to itercept the Jeep by which Dr. Salehuddin and Hirendra Chandra Roy were on the way towards Indian border to take refuge in India. With this, stopping the jeep the army men dragged them to the premises in front of the native house of former Chief Justice Syed AB Mahmud Hossain at Laskarpur through the bank of river 'Khoai' where they were hanged with a tree and were subjected to torture and after the dusk they were gunned down to death and their dead bodies were left abandoned near the house of one Ramjan Ali beside Laskarpur rail line. Therefore, accused Syed Md. Qaiser has been charged for substantially abetting, facilitating and contributing the actual commission of killing of 02 unarmed civilians constituting the offence of 'murder as crime against humanity' as specified in section 3(2)(a)(g)(h) of the Act which are punishable under 20(2) read with section 3(1) of the Act. And thus he incurred liability under section 4(1) of the Act."

 

289. In order to prove this charge, the prosecution examined 3 witnesses who are the PIW.2 Mohammad Ali Tipu, P.W.8 Shah Hossain Ali and P.W. 12 Gour Prosact Roy. The prosecution also produced the book “মুক্তিযুদ্ধে হবিগঞ্জ জেলা” written by Fazle Elahi material exhibit 'Ga" and “সিলেটের গণহত্যা” written by Tazul Islam.

 

290. P.W.2 Mohammad Ali Tipu in his testimony, stated that at about 3 to 3.30 p.m. on 29.04.1971, he, hearing the sound of firing, took shelter in a jungle of village Lenjapara. Thereafter, he went to Shaestaganj old market point and found a jeep, coming from Hobigonj town, going towards Chimarughat. At that time he found that some military vehicles were going towards the western side of old market. He saw that appellant Qaiser and Pakistani army getting down from those vehicles and pressurised Dr. Saleh Ahreed and Hiredndra Nath Roy to get down 'from their jeep. They were the local Awami League leaders Pakistani army, confining those two persons, brought them near Khoai bridge. Appellant Qaiser was with the Pakistani army at that time. In the evening, he came to know that Dr. Saleh Ahmed and Hirendra Nath Roy had been killed. In his cross examination, he denied the defence suggestion that in the occur-rence of killing of Saleh Ahmed and Hirendra Nath Roy appellant Qaiser Ali had no relation.

 

291. P.W. 8 Shah Hossain Ali, in his testimony in respect of charge No. 6, stated that he came to know that Qaiser, his banini , and Pakistani army had confined the Jeep of Dr. Saleh Ahmed and Hirendra Roy near Shaestaganj old bridge railway gate. They pressurised them to get down from the jeep and assaulted them. They brought the victims near river Khoai and killed them. P.W. 12 Gour Prosad Roy, in his testimony, stated that he saw the occurrence of confining the jeep carrying Dr. Saleh Ahmed and Hirendra Nath Roy. The appellant Qaiser and his bahini captured those two persons and got them down from the jeep. Appellant Qaiser disclosed the political identify of the victims Dr. Saleh Ahmed and Hirendra Nath Roy to Pak army. Thereafter, they assaulted the victims and compelled them to go towards Khoai Railway bridge. In his cross examination denied the defence suggestion that it is not true that statements made above are not true.

 

292. Mr. S.M. Shahjahan, submitted k that in the books namely, “মুক্তিযুদ্ধে হবিগঞ্জ জেলা” and “সিলেটের গণহত্যা” the authors did not state that at the time of taking down those two victims from the jeep appellant was present there so the testimonies of these three witnesses, namely, P.W.2, 8 and 12 are not reliable! The Tribunal committed error of law in convicting the appellant in this charge. On the other hand, learned Attorney General submits that P.W.2, 8 and 12 consistently deposed that they saw the occurrence of confining the victims by the Pak army and Qaiser and, thereafter, they were killed, the Tribunal did not commit any error in convicting the appellant in this charge.

 

293. It appears from the testimonies of P.Ws.2, 8 and 12 that they saw the occurrence of taking down the victims namely, Dr. Saleh Ahmed and Hirendra Nath Roy from their jeep by the Pak army at the instance of the appellant. They also stated that the appellant disclosed the identity of the victims to the Pakistani army that those two unarmed civilians were the local leaders of Awami League. Accordingly, Pakistani army confined them. Since these 3(three) witnesses corroborated each other saying that at the time of confinement of the victims the appellant was present and he disclosed the identity of the victims so they were compelled to get down from the jeep. It was unlikely for the Pakistan" army to know the identity of those two victims that they were local leaders of Awami League so the appellant is liable for confinement and abduction and, subsequent, killing. In view of those consistent evidence, we do not find any wrong in the conclusion arrived at by the Tribunal that the appellant was present at the time of confinement and abduction of those victims Dr. Saleh Ahmed and Hidrendra Nath Roy. From the books referred to by Mr. Shahjahan it appears 'that in those books it had been stated that Pakistan army confined the victims from the place of confinement as stated in the charge. It had not been stated that the appellant was not present with the army' at the time of confinement of the victims. In such view of the matter, the Tribunal rightly convicted the appellant on the basis of the testimonies of the P.Ws.2, 8 and 12. However, since the appellant was present at the time of confinement and abduction of those two unfortunate victims and disclosed the identity of the victims to the members of Pak army and that there is no evidence that he had passed the order to 'kill those two victims or at his instance of Pak army gunned them down, we are of the view, that proper sentence of the appellant in such circumstances in this charge would be to award sentence of imprisonment for life instead of sentence of death.

 

Charge No.7

 

294. "On 30 April 1971 in between 10:00-10:30 and 04:00-04:30 p.m., 10-15 members of 'Qaiser Bahini led by accused Syed Md. Qaiser being accompanied by the Pakistan occupation army arriving at Habiganj town created horror by launching attack and indiscriminate gun firing and started looting of house-holds of 40-45 civilians including Advocate Mostafa Ali MNA, Latifur Rahman @ Manik Chowdhury MNA, Dr. Abul Hashem MPA, Anil Kumar Roy, Iswar Paul, Roby Roy, Thakur Jhee, Sajib Ali, Surjakanta Babu, Rajaram, Upendra Paul and then with intent to destroy their property, set their houses and shops on fire. Therefore, accused Syed Md. Qaiser has been charged for abetting, facilitating and contributing the actual commission of the offence of 'other inhuman acts as crime against humanity' as specified in section 3(2)(a)(g)(h) of the Act which are punishable under section 20(2) read with section 3(1) of the Act. And thus he incurred liability under section 4(1) of the Act."

 

295. To prove charge No.7 against the appellant, the prosecution examined P.W.2 Mohammad Ali Tipu, P.W.7 Shah Hasan Ali and P.W.8 Shah Hossain Ali. It also relied upon the book “মুক্তিযুদ্ধে হবিগঞ্জ জেলা” written by Fazle Elahi.

 

296. P.W.2, in his testimony, in respect of charge No.7, stated that at about 9.45 to 10.00 a.m. on 30.04.1971 when military motor vehicles arrived at the area, he was staying in the house of Afsar Uddin. He saw 4/ 5 vehicles of Pakistani army standing in front of their house. He saw that Qaiser, some members of his bahini and members of Pakistani army got down from those vehicles and set fire to his house. Consequently, the dwelling house of this witness was burnt down. He also saw the flame of fire coming from the house of Manik Chowdhury. He came to know that in the evening, Pakistani army also burnt down the houses of Mostafa Shaheed, Anil Roy, father-in-law's house of Major C.R. Dutta, Dr. Hasim M.P. and houses and shops of some other persons of Habigonj town. In his cross examination, he denied the defence suggestion that it was not true that at the time of occurrence, the appellant and Pakistani army did not set fire to the houses of the persons mentioned above.

 

297. P.W. 7 Shah Hasan Ali, in his testimony, stated that on 30.04.1971, Pakistani army entered in Habigonj town and burnt down the houses of Mostafa Ali, Commandent Manik Chowdhury, Umesh Bhaban and some other houses and shops. At the relevant time, this witness was staying in his house situated near the house of Advocate Mostafa Ali. He saw the occurrence of setting fire and damaging those houses. In his cross examination, he denied that it is not true that the statement made above are not true.

 

298. P.W.8 Shah Hossain Ali is full brother of P.W.7 Shah Hasan Ali, in his testimony, stated that at about 10.00 to 11.00 a.m. op 30.04.1971, the Pakistan army, appellant and his bahini entered into Habigonj town damaged the hodses and sops including the house of Mostafa Ali.

 

299. Mr. S.M. Shahjahan Ali, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that in the book “মুক্তিযুদ্ধে হবিগঞ্জ জেলা” the author did not say that at the time of setting fire to the houses of Mostafa Ali and Commander4 Manik Chowdhury, the appellant Qaiser was present, so the appellant is entitled to get the benefit of doubt in respect of this charge.

 

300. Learned Attorney General, appearing for the respondent, submits that P.Ws. 2, 7 and 8 in their testimonies stated that the) saw that the appellant accompanied Pak army at the time of setting fire in different houses of Habigonj town, the Tribunal rightly believing the testimonies of P.Ws.2, 7 and 8, convicted the appellant.

 

301. It is not disputed that at about 10.00 to 11.00 a.m. on 30.04.1971 Pakistan, army entering into Habigonj town, set fire and destroyed some houses and shops. The only contention of the learned Advocate of the appellant is that appellant Qaiser did not accompany the members of Pak army at the time of set-ting fire in those houses and shops situated in Hobigonj town. But from the testimonies of P.Ws.2, 7 and 8 it appears that they saw that the appellant, accompanied by Pakistani army at the time of setting fire, looting and destroying the houses and shops of different persons of Habigonj town. The testimonies of P.Ws-.2, 7 and 8 are consistent in that regard. In view of the consistent evidence, we do not find anything wrong in the conclusion arrived at by the Tribunal that Pakistan army and the appellant burnt, destroyed and looted the houses and shops of Mostafa Ali and also the houses of Manik Chowdhury, father-in-law of Major C.R. Dutta and some other persons in Hobigonj town.

 

302. Accordingly, we do not find any wrong in the conclusion arrived at by the Tribunal.

 

Charge No.8.

 

303. "On 11th May, 1971, at about 10:00 am accused Syed Md. Kaiser and a group of Pakistan occupation army rushed towards Chanpur tea garden under Chunarughat Police Station of the then Habiganj sub-division and on arriving there that group started causing torture to the garden labourers and dwellers belonging to Hindu community and, at a stage, entered into the dwelling but of one Sautal woman Hiramoni and on accused's showing and asking 2-3 army men committed rape upon Hiramoni. Therefore, accused Syed Md. Kaiser has been charged for substantially abetting, facilitating and contributing the actual commission of sexual ravishment upon one sautal woman constituting the offence of 'rape as crime against humanity' which was part of attack against civilian population as specified in section 3(2) (a)(g)(h) of the Act which are punishable under section 20(2) read with section 3(1) of the Act and thus accused incurred liability under section 4(1) of the Act."

 

304. In order to prove Charge No.8, the prosecution examined two witnesses, P.W.18 Basu Sautal and P.W. 20 Abdul Motaleb. Of them, P.W.18 stated that in the last part of Boishak, perhaps it was May, 11, 1971, his elder brother Bipin and he himself were staying in the house his Pishi (father's sister) at her dwelling hut. At that time his Pisha went outside the house. At about 10 a.m., after having breakfast, he was sitting in the courtyard and his Pishi was working in her kitchen. At that time, Gafur, Abdul Haque and two Pakistani army personnel entered into their house along with another Bengali man wearing civil dress. This witness took shelter behind a bush and saw that the civil dressed man gave signal to Pakistani army personnel to enter into the house of his Pisi. Accordingly, those two members of Pakistan army entered into the house of his Pishi Hiramony Sautal. Thereafter, his Pishi raised alarm seeking help to save her. His grandfather Bipin rushed there to rescue his Pishi but they resisted them. Gafur and Abdul Haque assaulted his grandfather who raised alarm. Thereafter, he did not hear any sound of his Pishi. This witness returned to the house after leaving Pakistan army personnel and those persons and found that Pakistan army had raped upon her Pishi. In the afternoon, local people went there and disclosed that the person wearing white print shirt was Qaiser Ali of village Nowapara. He denied the defence suggestion that it was not true that the occurrence did not take place in the manner stated above.

 

305. P.W.20 Abdul Motaleb in his testimony stated that on 11th or 12th May, 1971, at 9.00 a.m. he went to the Dolna Tea Garden and, found Pakistani army in 5 different vehicles in that Garden. They got down from vehicles. He identified Major Sher Bahadur, Major Yousuf, and appellant Qaiser. Sher Bahadur called this witness. Appellant told Sher Bahadur that this witness was a freedom, fighter. Major Yousuf and Sher Bahadur replied that this witness is a good man.

 

In 1965 War, Sher Bahadtir took shelter in his house. Thereafter, Pakistan army moved towardS Chandpur through their vehicle's taking the witness with them. Appellant Qaiser, Major Yousuf and some members of Pakistani army stopped their vehicles near Chandpur Chagolbazaar. Appellant Qaiser Ali and two other Bengalee and Pakistani army went to a tea garden. Then this witness asked Major Yousuf what he would do. Who rekliecr that he may leave the area. This witness took shelter in a sugarcane field situated behind the house of Hiramoni Sautal. He was not previously acquainted Hiramoni Sautal. He heard the sound of outcry from the house of Hiramoni Sautal. An old man tried to protect her. At that time, the appellant Qaiser and two other Bengalee people assaulted him. This witness went to the house of Hiramoni Sautal and found that she was crying. He came to know that Pakistani army, at the instance of appel-lant, entered in to the house of Hiramoni Sautal and raped upon her. In his cross examination, he denied that it is not true that in the War of 1965 Major Yousuf and Sher Bahadur took shelter in his house.

 

306. Mr. S.M. Shahjahan, in his submission 'contended that the P.W.20 was a chance witness and P.W. 8 was minor at the time of occurrence. So, their testimonies are not reliable.

 

307. In this case victim Hiramoni had not been examined. However, it appears from the materials on record that, at present, she has been suffering from various diseases. It has not been denied that victim Hiramoni was not raped by the Pakistani army. The P.W.1 8 in his testimony stated that previously he was not acquainted with the appellant but he identified the appellant and said that he gave signal to the army personnel who, thereafter, entered into the house of victim and raped her. That is, at the time of commission of rape upon Hiramoni the appellant accompanied those two members of Pak army. Evidence of P.W.1 8 and 20 in this regard are consistent particularly, P.W.20 is a disinterested wit-ness who corroborated the testimony of P. W.1 8. As a human being it, was the duty of the appellant to obstruct the rapists. Unfortunately, he did not do so. Rather it is evident that he instigated those two members of the Pakistan army by giving signal. Looking on such inhuman activities of Pakistan army, this appellant did not make any obstruction. The charge against this appellant that he aided and instigated those two members of the Pakistani army to commit rape upon the victim Hiramoni Sautal has been proved by P.Ws 18 and 20.

 

308. Considering the facts, circumstances and evidence, we are of the view that proper sentence of the appellant in this charge would he to suffer imprisonment for life instead of sentence of death.

 

Charge No.9

 

309. "On 15 May 1971, between 10:00-10:30 am' and 01:00-01:30 p.m. accused Syed Md. Qaiser, leader of `Qaiser Bahini', being accompanied by his 10-15 companions Razakar force and a group of 30 members of Pakistani armed force moved towards the village Tohaid' under Madhabpur police station, the then Habiganj subdivision where they launching attack apprehended pro-liberation civilians namely (1) Abdul Aziz, (2) Abdul Gafur, (3) Jamiruddin, (4) Azimuddin, (5) Etimunnesa, (6) Nur Ali, (7) Alamchan Bibi, (8) Abdul Ali from their respective houses and then following accused's instruction the army men caused their death by charging bayonet and gun shot. The perpetrators committed looting of Rahimuddin's house and then set it on fire. Therefore, accused Qaiser has been charged for abetting, facilitating and substantially contributing the actual commission of killing of 08 unarmed civilians constituting the offence of 'murder as crime against humanity' as specified in section 3(2)(a)(g)(h) of the Act which are punishable under section 20(2) read with section 3(1) of the Act and thus liable under section 4(1) of the Act. And thus he incurred liability under section 4(1) of the Act."

 

310. It appears that the charge against the appellant is that on 15th May, 1971 the appellant with his bahini and members of Pak army surrounded the village of Lohaid under the Madhabpur Police Station and launched attacks upon unarmed civilians and killed (1) Abdul Aziz, (2) Abdul Gafur, (3) Jamiruddin, (4) Azimuddin, (5) Etimunnesa, (6) Nur Ali, (7) Alamchan Bibi and (8) Abdul Ali.

 

311. To prove the charge against the appellant, the prosecution examined 3(three) witnesses, namely, P.W. 17 Md. Ful Miah, P.W.21 Md. Omar Ali and P.W. 22 Md. Lokman Hossain.

 

312. Of them, P.W. 17 Md. Ful Miah, was a student of class ten in 1971. In his testimony, he stated that at about 10.00 to 10.30 a.m. on 15.05.1971, he saw Pakistan army and Rajakers in two vehicles stopped at northern side of a broken culvert of Nowahati to Darmager road. He saw that 15/16 Pakistani army and 10/12 persons wearing Police dress and 2(two) civil dressed persons got down from those two vehicles. Out of those two persons, one was Langra Hamid, another was Syed Qaiser. This witness, at the relevant time, was standing on the bank of "Razarmar Dighi". Thereafter, he heard the sound of firing from the house of Abdul Aziz and Jamir Uddin who were his "fupa". He also heard the sound of firing from the village Lohaid. Thereafter, he saw the Pakistani army and "Qaiser bahini" returning to their vehicles and, then, left the place. This witness found that villagers, Lockman, Hossain Ali and Omar were running towards Indian border. They told that Pakistani army and "Qaiser bahini" had killed Abul Aziz, Abdul Gafur, Jamir Uddin, Etimunnesaa, Nur Ali Chowdhury, Alamchand Bibi and Abdul Ali. This witness then rushed to the village Lohaid along with others and found the dead bodies of those unarmed civilians. They buried the victims. At that time, Mahbub Uddin Chowdhury told that he saw appellant Qaiser and his bahini with Pakistani army. He hiding himself in a mango grove saw the occurrence. In his cross examination he denied the defence suggestion that he did not see the aforesaid occurrence of village Lohaid.

 

313. P.W. 21 Md. Omar Ali was aged about 17/18 years in 1971. In his testimony, he stated that at about 10.00-10.30 a.m. on 14'1' or 15th May, 1971, he was having his meal in the house of one Kazi Nur Ali. At that time, Nur Ali told him that Pakistani army had arrived in'the village. Pakistani army and Qaiser entered into the house of one Khaleque who took shelter under the "paddy dola" and saw that Pakistani army, who were 14 to 15 in number, and appellant Qaiser were standing in their courtyard. One Nur Ali" offered "salam" to Qaiser but Qaiser, without offering reply to his salam, gave signal to Pak army personel. Then Pakistani army shot, Nur Ali who died on the spot. Akram Ali Chowdhury, "khalu" of This witness, who had been suffering from Paralyses, was also killed. Qaiser Ali was standing with Pakistani army in that courtyard at the relevant time. At about 1.30 p.m. "Qaiser bahini" and Pakistani army left the village. Thereafter, this witness visited the village and found the dead bodies of Adul Aziz, Abdul Gafur, Jamir Uddin, Eatimunessa and Abdul Ali. In his cross examination, he stated that the statements made above are not true. He also denied that at the instance of Kazi Rakibuddin he has deposed falsely.

 

314. P.W.22 Md. Lokman Hossain was aged about 17 years in 1971. In his testimony, he stated that after having breakfast on 15th May, 1971 he went in search of his maternal uncle Abdul Jabbar near Primary school and found that Abdul Jabbar, keeping his cattle-head in the field, was running towards their village. This witness asked him about the cause of his running who replied that Pakistani army was coming towards their village. This witness returned to his house and found the villagers running towards Indian border. This witness took shelter beneath the heep of paddy straw situated at the south western corner of his house. He heard the sound of firing. He saw appellant Qaiser, some Bengalee and members of Pakistani army standing in front of the house of Abdul Gat/it They killed Gofur on the spot. At 1.30 p.m. Pakistani army left the village. Then this witness came out from the heap of paddy straw and saw the dead bodies of the victims. He visited the village and found P.W.21 Omar All and P.W. 17 Ful Miah. They buried those unfortunate victims. In his cross examination, he denied that appellant Qaiser was not present with the Pakistani army at the time of com-mission of the aforesaid occurrence. He also denied that the statements made above are not true. He also denied the defence suggestion that at the instance of Kazi Kabiruddin he has deposed falsely.

 

315. Mr. S.M. Shahjahan, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that the testimonies of these three witnesses are weak type of evidence and 'order of conviction relying upon the testimonies of those witnesses is unsafe. On the other hand, learned Attorney General appearing for the State, submits that all of those three witnesses are eye witnesses of the occurrence and they corroborated each others as to tiny, place and manner of occurrence committed on 15th May, 1971 in the village Lohaid.

 

316. It appears from the testimonies of the three witnesses namely, P. W.17 Ful Miah, P.W.21 Md. Omar Ali and P.W. 22 Md. Lokman Hossain that all of these witnesses categorically stated that at about 10.00 -10.30 a.m. on 15th May, 1971 Pakistani army, "Qaiser bahini" and appellant himself surrounded the village Lohaid and discriminately killed the aforesaid unarmed civilians. All these three witnesses in their testimonies' stated that Syed Qaiser himself was present there at the time of killing those unfortunate civilians. We do not find any contradictions and discrepancies in the evidence of P.Ws. 17, 21 and 22 which create any doubt about the time, place and manner the killing of the victims and involvement of the appellant in that occurrence. In such view of the matter, we do not find any illegality in awarding conviction and sentence of the appellant in this charge by the Tribunal.

 

Charge No.10

 

317. "On 13 June 1971 at about 2:00-03:00 pm on instruction of accused Syed Md. Qaiser being the' leader of `Qaiser Bahini', members of Qaiser Bahini and Razakar force forcibly picked up local organiser of liberation war Shah Firoz Mia from his house at Mokambari locality under Habiganj police Station district Habiganj and on capture he was first brought to Habiganj police station where he was kept confined for one night and on the following day he was-brought to Shaestaganj R&H Dukbangalow where accused Syed Md. Qaiser handed him over to the Pakistani army."

 

318. From the charge No.10, it appears that "Qaiser bahini" picked up one Shah Firoz from his house of village Mokambari and kept him confined in the lock up of Habigonj Police Station and, on the next day, the appellant Qaiser handed over the victim Shah Firoz to Pakistan army.

 

319. In order to prove this charge, the prosecution examined two witnesses. They are P.W. 7 Shah Hasan Ali and P.W.8 Shah Hossain Ali. They also produced a book, material exhibit "Ja" namely, “সিলেটের গণহত্যা” written by Tazul Islam.

 

320. Of them, P.W.7 Shah Hasan Ali, son of victim Firoz Ali was a student of class nine of J.K. and H. High School in 1971. In his testimony, he stated that on 13th June, 1971 at about 2.00 to 2.30 p.m. his father Shah Firoz Ali, after having his meal, was talking to other inmates of his house. This witness was also present there. All on a sudden, Soleman Razakar, Abul Thikadar and some others rushed to their house called his father saying that Qaiser Saheb had called him staying in the house of Barek Mokhter. His father asked about the reason of such calling and denied to go with them. Those miscreants confining him compelled to go with them through a rickshaw van. Uncles of this witness other Inmates and this witness saw that occurrence of confinement and abduction of victim Shah Firoz. Shah Abdul Hai and Babor Ali Miah and this witness followed them and found that those Rajakars were going towards Habigonj instead of going to the house of Barek Mokter. They went to Habigonj Sadar Police Station. This witness found appellant Qaiser, Barek Moktar, Soleman Razakar and Abul Thikadar sitting at Habigonj Police station. Uncles of this witness, namely, Shah Nur Ali, Shah Abdul Hai and Babor Ali repeatedly requested Qaiser Ali and Barek Moktar to release the victim Shah Firoz but they directed them to bring their nephew and to handover his arms to them and threatened them saying that, otherwise, they would hand over the victim to Pakistan army. This witness and his uncle returned home and disclosed the same to the inmates to their house. His father was severely tortured throughout the whole night in the morning of 14th June, 1971, they went to the Police Station and found the victim injured. At about 7.00 p.m. Qaiser, Barek Moker, Abul Thikadar and others, taking the victim Shah Firoz Ali in a jeep, went towards the Saestaganj Pak army camp and handed over him to army people. This witness and his uncles returned home. In the afternoon, Nur Ali, uncle of this witness, again went to Sayestagonj and after returning home he told that the victim Shah Firoz was assaulted severely fastening with a pillar of Dakbanglow of Shaestagonj. He found Qaiser, Barek Moktar and some others at Dakbanglow. Pakistan army, taking the victim Shah Firoz and some other abducted persons, went to Sreemongal. His uncle and he himself saw that occurrence. Nur Ali, uncle of this witness requested Qaiser, Barek Mokter to release victim Shah Firoz but they did not pay any heed. The victim is still untraced. This witness further stated that his brother, got information that his father had been killed by the Pakistan army. His brother freedom fighter Shah Hossain Ali returned home in the evening of 16 July, 1971 and heard about the occurrence of killing of his father from the inmates of their house. When his mother was giving meal to Shah Hossain Ali, all on a sudden, Soleman Razakar and other members of "Qaiser Bahini" surrounded their house-and started calling his brother who did not respond. Then Razakar bahini, breaking the door of their house, confined Shah Hossain Ali and kept him confined at Shahjibazar army camp for about 20/25 days. They tortured him severely. After getting release from army camp he took treatment. In course of treatment, the doctors removed his left leg. On 16th December, 1971 they went to Sreemongal killing spot to search his father but did not find him. They found, hundreds of dead bodies lying in the killing spot of Sreemongal. In his cross examination, he denied that the statements made above by this witness are not true. He also denied, that he was not previously acquainted with Sayed Qaiser and at the instance of Kazi Kabiruddin, Mohammad Ali Pathan, Mohammad Ali Tipu he has deposed falsely.

 

321. P.W.8 Shah Hossain Ali, another son of victim Shah Firoz Ali., is a disabled freedom fighter. He went to India and took training as freedom fighter. On 13-06-1971, he came to know 'from Commander Younus Chowdhury that Qaiser bahini had abducted his father and, thereafter, appellant Qaiser and Barek Moktar had handed over his father Shah Firoz to the Pakistan army. Getting such information from Younus Chowdhury, he met Mostafa Ali and expressed his desire to return home. After getting permission from his commander, he returned home on 10th or 11th July, 1971. His uncles Shah Noor Ali, Abdul Hai and Shah Babur Ali and other inmates of his house told him that Soleman Razakar, Ramiz Razakar, Abul Thikadar and 10 /12 confining his father went to local police station. His uncle and younger brother Shah Hasan Ali (P.W.7) followed them and found Qaiser and Barek Moktar in the room of the Officer-in-Charge of Police Station and kept his father confined in the lock up.

 

They requested repeatedly to release the victim Shah Firoz but they did not pay any heed saying that before getting this witness, who was a freedom fighter, they would not hand over the victim. Uncle of this witness met Syed Quamral Hasan, local leader of Nezami Islam, requested him to request Qaiser and Barek member to release his father. Appellant Qaiser told that he would not release the victim. They further told that on 14th June, 1971 members of Qaiser Bahini handed over Shah Feroz to Pakistan army camped at Shaestaganj Dakbanglow. Nur Ali, uncle of this witness, went there and found the victim fastened with a pillar of Dakbanglow. They also found Qaiser, Barek Moktar, Abul Thikadar and Soleman Razakar. At about 3/ 4 p.m. Qaiser and Pakistan army, taking Shah Feroz, went to Sreemongal. At that time, one shopkeeper told that the victims, who were sent to Sreemongal, did never return. This witness further stated that after hearing the aforesaid facts, his mother gave him dinnei. At that time, Soleman Razakar, Ramiz Razakar and Shafiq went to their house and started calling him. His uncle, his younger brother hid him under a "Chowki". Those rajakars broke up the door but caught this witness and fastened his eyes and thereafter taking him went to local police station. He found the appellant, Barek Mokter, Romiz and Soleman in the room of the O.C. of the Police Station. Qaiser himself asked above particulars of other freedom fighters. He replied that he simply went to India. At that time, Qaiser and Barek Mokter told him to join Razakarpahini. This witness replied that he would not join in Razakar Bahini. In the night, they handed over this witness to Army camped at Shastaganj. On 17 July, at about 10.00 a.m. Qaiser, Barek Moktar, Abul Thikadar, Soleman and 4/5 other went to Shaestaganj Dakbanglow. At that time, Qaiser asked the Army personnel as to why this witness had not yet been killed. In the afternoon, they brought this witness to Shaestaganj Railway Station and brought him at Sahjibazar through train. They kept him confined in a room of Semi pucca tin shed at Shahjibazar. On the next day, Pakistani army tortured this witness inhumanly. Members of "Qaiser bahini" also tortured this witness. They tortured this witness continuously for about 20/ 25 days. One of the members of Pakistani army, considering the health condition of this witness, told him that he would request Major Bahadur Shah to get release from confinement. Major Bahadtir Shah, considering the marks of torturing on the person of this witness, decided to release him. Thereafter, he was released. He returned his home and took treatment. At the time of deposing, this witness started crying in the witness box. He identified the accused on dock. In his cross examination he said that he had lodged a case against Syed Qaiser in 1972. He denied the defence suggestion that the statements made above are not true. He also denied that there was no existence of "Qaiser bahini". He also denied that at the instance of P.W.1 he has deposed falsely.

 

322. Mr. S.M. Shahjahan, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that there is no evidence that victim Shah Firoz was killed in 1971 and the appellant had any complicity in the occurrence stated in this charge.

 

323. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney General, appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that P.W.7, found appellant Qaiser at local Police Station. His Qaiser bahini, after abducting victim Shah Feroz, brought him at the local Police Station at the instance of Qaiser. His uncle in presence of this witness requested the appellant to release him who did not pay any heed. He also saw the occurrence of fastening the victim with a pillar of Shaestagonj Dakbanglow and, since then, the victim Feroj Shah is missing. The P.W.8 categorically stated that since he was a freedom tighter, the members of "Qaiser bahini" abducted his father Shah Feroj in the presence of P.W.7 other members of his family and directed him to produce P.W.B. He submits that there is no cogent reason to disbelieve P.W.7.

 

324. From the testimony of P.W.8, it appears that at the time of abduction of victim Shah Firoz, this witness was not present in his house. He heard from P.W.7 and others that the members of Qaiser Bahini, confining Shah Feroz, to the local Police Station. However, P.W.7 in his testimony categorically stated that he and his uncle followed Qaiser bahini and found that they went to local Police Station. P.W.7 found the appellant Qaiser sitting at the local Police Station who went there along with his uncle. His uncle requested appellant Qaiser to release the victim Shah Firoz but the appellant did not pay any heed rather the appellant directed his uncle to produce the P.W.8 (freedom fighter) to than. P.W.7 also stated that, on the next day, he went to Shaestagonj Dakbanglow again where he found that his father was fastened with a pillar of Dakbanglow. He also found appellant Qaiser present at Dakbanglow. Since then his father is found to be untraced. While getting such information, P.W.8, who was freedom fighter and brother of P.W.7 and son of victim Shah Firoz, returned home from India and heard about the story of abduction of victim Shah Firoz from his uncle and P.W.7. P.W.7 in his testimony said that he told the story of abduction of his father to his brother P.W.B. Members of "Qaiser bahini" surrounded' his house and confined P.W.8 in the night when his mother was serving dinner to him. These two witnesses, at the time of deposing in the Tribunal, became emotional and started crying. From the facts, circumstances and the evidence adduced by the P.Ws. 7 and 8, we do not find any reason to disbelieve their testimonies. Of them, P.W.7 himself was the witness of abduction and confinement of the victim Shah Firoz. He and his uncle repeatedly requested appellant Qaiser for getting release of victim Shah Firoz but without releasing him they handed over the victim to Pakistani army.

 

325. Considering the facts, circumstances and the evidence adduced, by the prosecution, we are of the view that the Tribunal rightly observed that the prosecution has been able to prove this charge against the appellant beyond reasonable doubt. However, since there is no evidence that appellant Qaiser himself abducted and had killed victim Shah Firoz, we are of the view that justice would best be done to the appellant if he is awarded sentence to suffer imprisonment for life instead of sentence of death.

 

Charge No.11

 

326. "On 23rd June 1971 at about 10:30-11:00 am. a. group of 40-50 armed members of 'Qaiser Bahini' and Razakar force led by accused Syed Md. Qaiser by attacking the house of Golam Nur, an organizer of liberation war of village Haripur under Police Station Naisrnagar, sub-division Brahamanbaria, looted the households and set the house on fire and abducted Golam Rouf there from and brought him at his [Qaiser] house at Noapara and kept him detained there for one week where he was subjected to torture. He was released in exchange of taka 8,000/00. But Golam Rasul Master died two weeks after the severe torture caused to him."

 

327. From the charge, it appears that the allegations brought against the appellant was that appellant and his bahini attacking the house of P.W.13 Golam Nur, bunit down his house and, abducting his father Golam Rouf, kept him confinement in the house of the appellant Qaiser at Nowapara, and, thereafter, receiving a sum of taka 8000/-released him.

 

328. In support of this charge, the prose-cution examined P.W.1, Kazi Kabiruddin, P.W. 3 Tajul Islam, P.W.13 Golam Nur, P.W.15 Nisha Mon, P.W.16 Abdul Matin and P. W.31 Azaharul Haque.

 

329. P. W.1 in his testimony stated that he got information that Qaiser bahini and Pakistani army had burnt down the house of Golam Nur of village Haripur under Nasirnagar. Police Station and on the same day they also set fire to the house of Sayedul Haque. P.W.3 Tazul Islam in his testimony stated that as per direction of Qaiser, on 23rd June, 1971, 100 members of his bahini surrounded the house of Golam Nur and pursuant to the direction of Qaiser, they set fire to the house of Golam Nur. When Golam Rouf Master, brother of Golam Nur came out from his house Qaiser directed his bahini to confine him, accordingly, members of his bahini fastened him. Father of Golam Rouf, his mother and Bhabi requested Qaiser to release him. Qaiser and his bahini, confining Golam Rouf went to the house of Monjour Ali of village Goniaok. Situ Mia and Tota Miah met Qaiser and requested him to release Golam Rouf but he did not pay any heed. Thereafter, Montu Miah, father-in-law of Golam Rouf, handed over a letter to Qaiser Ali and then, Qaiser released Golam Rouf. In his cross examination, this witness denied the defence suggestion that the statements made above are not true. P. W.13 Golam Nur in his testimony stated that he came to know from his mother, brother and bhabi that on 23rd June, 1971 at about 10.00 to 10.30 p.m. Qaiser and his bahini, entering into his house, set fire and assaulted his brother and father. At that time his mother, bhabi and sister took shelter in a pond. His bhabi told that Qaiser, confining his brother, left the place towards the east. At that time, his maternal uncle and brother's father-in-law went to the house of Manzur Ali Of village Goniauk but did not find his brother. He also came to know that Qaiser taking his brother went to his village Nawapara. He also came to know that Qaiser and his bahini set fare to the house of Advocate Sayedul Hague. 5/6 days thereafter Qaiser released his brother upon getting payment of taka 8000/-and receiving a letter from Monzur Ali.

 

In his cross examination, he denied the defence suggestion that the statements made above are not true. He' also denied that he has deposed falsely.

 

330. P.W.15 Nisha Mon, in his testimony, stated that on 84h Asar, 1971 at about 10.00 to 11.00 a.m. her husband and she was having breakfast. At that time, Qaiser and his bahini entered into their dwelling hut. She shut the door. At one stage, she tried to flee away but Qaiser and his bahini confined her, 'asked about the whereabouts Golam Nur who replied that she was not aware about the whereabouts of Nur. Then Qaiser assaulted her. At the relevant time, Qaiser was in civil dress and other members of his bahini were wearing brown coloured dress. This witness earlier was acquainted with Qaiser since his maternal uncle's house is at village Guniak. She knew Tazul Islam, a member of Qaiser Bahini since his house is situated near the house of this witness. When the father-in-law of this witness went to get her husband released then Qaiser asked about the whereabouts of his son Golam Nur who replied that he was not conversant with his whereabouts. At that time, this witness and her mother-in-law begged to get release of her husband and father-in-law from Qaiser and his bahini. Qaiser assaulted this witness. This witness further stated that Qaiser and his bahini set fire to their homestead, consequently, 8 cattleheads were burnt down. Thereafter, Qaiser and his bahini left the place. She also found her father-in-law lying on the ground in a position about to die. This witness, her mother-in-law and children went to her father's house at village Chithna and described her father about the brutality committed by Qaiser.

 

Hearing so, her father went to the house of Monzur Ali master, maternal uncle of Qaier of village Guniak where from she went to the village of Qaiser at Nawapara but did not find Golam Rouf. At the time of returning home, her father found that "Qaiser bahini" had set fire to the houses of village Gutma and looted bash and kinds therefrom. Her father saw that Golam Rouf was fastene4rith a Mango tree. He requested Qaiser to release the victim Golam Rouf but Qaiser, threatening him compelled to leave that place who returned home and disclosed that fact to the inmates of the house. On the next day, father of this witness, maternal mother-in-law went to Nawapara and requested Qaiser to release Golam Rouf who demanded taka 10,000/- for getting release. Thereafter, father of this witnesses and maternal mother in law went to the house of maternal uncle of Qaiser and taking a letter from him and collecting taki 8000/- again went to the Nawapara and met Qaiser. Receiving that letter and money Qaiser released the victim Golam Rouf. In her cross examination, this witness stated that she is an illiterate woman. She denied the defence sugges-tion that it is not true that the statements made above are not true.

 

331. P.W.16 Abdul Matin in his testimony stated that on 23rd June, 1971 at about 10.00 to 10.30 a.m. Qaiser and his bahini went to the house of Golam Nur. At that time, Golam Nur went to India to participate in the war of independence. They assaulted his father Golam Rasul, brother of Golam Rouf, mother and brother's wife and set fire to their house. Consequently, the house of Golam Nur was destroyed and their cattleheads were burnt. At one stage, Qaiser and his bahi-ni confining Golam Rouf went to the house of his maternal uncle at Goniak. This witness saw the occurrence from hiding. Some times thereafter, Qaiser and his bahini taking Golam Rouf left the place towards north. At about 2.00 to 2.30 p.m., they came to know that Qaiser and his bahini had set fire to the house of Badal Karmaker and looted goods there from. They fastened Gobinda Karmaker and Golam Rouf with a mango tree. They also burnt the house of Sayedul Haque setting fire. This witness heard about the said occurrence. In his cross examination he said that he does not know who were The President and the Secretary of Nasirnagar Awami League at the relevant time. He contended that village Guniak is about 21/2 miles away from Haripur. He denied the defence suggestion that aforesaid facts are not true.

 

332. P.W.31 Azharul Haque in his testimony stated that on 23rd" June, 1971 at about 4.00 p.m he saw flame of fire from the house of Sayedul Hague and heard about story of setting fire from the people fleeing away. They told this Witness that Qaiser and his bahini had set fire to the house of Sayedul Haque. He also came to know that Qaiser and his bahini also caused damage the house of Golam Nur upon setting fire. This witness went to the house of Golam Nur and found aforesaid facts are true. He also found the condition of the father of Golm Nur is precarious. In his cross examination, he told that his elder brother took training from different camps in India. He further stated that in June, 1971 the area was flood affected. He further said that water of flood recorded from the area inthe middle of October.

 

333. Mr. S.M. Shahjahan, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that the evidence of prosecution witnesses are contradictory as to the time, place and manner of occurrence which has made the prosecution case doubtful so this appellant is entitled , to get benefit of doubt in respect of the charge.

 

334. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learped Attorney General appearing on behalf of State, submits that the eye witnesses P.W.13 and 15 corroborated each other as to the time, manner and place of occurrence as committed by the appellant on 23rd June, 1971. The tribunal upon proper assessment of evidence convicted the appellant in this charge.

 

335. In order to prove this charge prosecution examined P.W.3 1, Md. Azaharul Haque who in his cross examination has said “১৯৭১ সালে আমাদের এলাকায় জুন মাসে বর্ষার পানি এসেছিল” He further said “বর্ষার পানি অক্টোবরের মাঝামাঝি আমাদের এলাকা থেকে নেমে যেত। আমাদের এলাকার সর্বদক্ষিণে এবং সর্ব উত্তরে নভেম্বরের মাঝামাঝি সময়ে হালকা কিছু পানি থাকতো”

 

P.W. 13 Nisha Mon in her cross examination has said “ইহা সত্য যে, আমার শ্বশুর বাড়ী এলাকায় আষাঢ় মাসে মাঠ ঘাটে পানি আসে।” That is, both the witnesses in their testimony stated that in the month of Asar, the area was watery. P.W. 13 in her testimony once stated that “আমি প্রাণ ভয়ে শ্বাশুড়ী, ননদসহ কোলের বাচ্চা নিয়ে আমার ঘরের উত্তরের পুকুরে গলা পর্যন্ত ডুবে প্রাণ রক্ষা করার চেষ্টা করি।” But she again claimed that she saw every activities of Qaiser and his bahini. P. W.13 Nisha Mon in her cross examination has said that she never went to village Nawapara and she is not aware where village Nawapara is situated and under what Police Station. It is evident that Nawapara, Habigoni is 50 miles away from Nasirnagar Police Station of the then B. Baria Sub-Division. In view of the aforesaid evidence, it is difficult to rely upon the testimonies of P.W.13, 15 and 31 as to the date and manner of occurrence committed on 23rd June, 1971 at village Haripur, Nashirnagar since area at the relevant time was watery and the distance between the village of the appellant and place of occurrence is about 50 miles. Considering the facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the appellant is entitled to get benefit of doubt since it is doubtful whether the offence as enumerated in this charge was committed in the stated date and manner.

 

Charge No.12

 

336. "On any day of mid August Of 1971 [end of Bangla month Sraban] at noon accused Syed Md. Qaiser accompanied by members of 'Qaiser Bahini' and Razakar force, brought Majeda. Begiiin, her father Atab Mia and uncle Ayub Mia to the army camp set up at Jagadishpur High School under Madhabpur Police Station on capture from their house and then accused Syed Md. Qaiser handed Majeda Begum over to the army for their entertainment, despite protest on her father's part. The army men thus committed recurrent rape upon Majeda, during night for 8/10 days and later on, physically and mentally devastated Majeda who was left abandoned at a place near Temunia Primary School wherefrom she managed to return home somehow and received necessary medical treatment and few days later she felt her pregnancy that resulted from the forcible sexual invasion to her at the army camp. Therefore, accused Syed Md. Qaiser has been charged for substantially abetting, facilitating and contributing the actual commission of committing forcible sexual ravishment constituting the offence of 'rape' as crime against humanity as specified in section 3(2)(a)(g)(h) of the Act of 1973 which are punishable under section 20(2) read with section 3(1) of the Act and thus the accused incurred liability under section 4(1) of the Act."

 

337. From Charge No.12, it appears that the allegations against the appellant is that the appellant abetted, facilitated and contributed Pakistani army for commission of recurrent rape upon Mazeda Begom keeping her confined in army camp of Jagadispur High School. In support of charge, the prosecution examined 3 (three) witnesses. They are P. W.1 Kazi Kabiruddin, P.W. 5 Majeda Begum and P. W.10 Shamsun Nahar.

 

338. Of them, P.W. 1 in his testimony stated that 2(two) years after the war of independence, he met Mahbub Uddin Chowdhury, an accused of Agortola conspiracy case and freedom fighter Matin. Mahbub Uddin Chowdhury told this witness that Mazeda Begum (P.W.5), brother's daughter of Matin, was confined by appellant Syed Qaiser during the war of Liberation and he handed over her to Pak army camped at Jogodishpur High School where she was victim of recurrent rape committed by some members of Pak army. 'Qaiser himself was involved in such recurrent raping. Consequently, Mazeda became pregnant and, ultimately, gave birth to a baby girl. In such circumstances, her husband Alai Miah denied accepting her. Mazeda Begum was given in marriage to Alai Miah 3(three) days before starting the war of Liberation. Mahbub Uddin Chowdhury requested this witness to convince Alai Miah so that he permits victim Mazeda Begum to stay in his house. Thereafter, Mahbub Uddin Chowdhury and this witness requested Alai Miah who, then, agreed to accept Mazeda Begum.

 

339. Victim Mazeda Begum was examined as P.W.5 who, in her testimony, stated that in the month of Sraban her father, uncle and she were taking their meal. At that time, "Qaiser bahini" and 10/11 members of Razakar bahini entered into their dwelling homestead asked her father about the whereabouts of her uncle Matin. Her father replied that he was not conversant about his whereabouts. At that time, members of "Qaiser bahini" started beating her father. This witness, looking so, raised alarm and started crying. Then the members of "Qaiser bahini" confined her, her father and uncle and brought them to the army camp of Jagadispur High School where she found appellant Qaiser. The members of "Qaiser bahini" handed over them to Qaiser. This witness found 7/8 other women confined there. Qaiser bahini surrounded them. At that time, appellant Qaiser himself handed over this victim to Pakistani army. He asked the father and uncle of this victim about her another uncle, namely, Matin. But they did not disclose any information about Matin to them. Then appellant Qaiser directed the members of his bahi-ni to compel her father, and uncle of this witness to excavate a ditch. Pursuant to the order, father and uncle of this witness and 10/15 others excavated a ditch. Then 2(two) members of Razakars bahini threw this witness in that ditch. In the evening, fatter of this victim requested Qaiser bahini to release this witness but he did not pay any heed. Qaiser compelled the father and uncle of this witness to leave the place. In the evening, when it was raining, "Qaiser bahini" brought this witness from ditch and kept her confined in a room of that army camp. Thereafter, members of Pakistani army one after another committed rape upon her. She started crying. Then mem-bers of Pakistani army put a piece of cloth in her mouth. Members of Pakistani army committed recurrent rape upon her one after another keeping her confined 8/10 days. Consequently, this witness became seriously ill. In such a situation, Qaiser directed the members of his bahini to throw this witness elsewhere. This witness herself heard such utterance from the mouth of Qaiser. Appellant Qaiser, directed them to throw out this witness to the field of Jogodishpur Primary School and, accordingly, she was thrown in that field. This victim was laying on the ground througout the whole night. In the morning, she had been able to reach his father's house. At the time of deposing before the Tribunal this victim started crying. Due to recurrent rape, this wit-ness became pregnant and, ultimately, she gave birth of a female child who was named Shamsunahar (P.W.10). Her husband dehied to accept this witness. Freedom fighter Advocate Matin, uncle of this witness, Farid, freedom fighter Awal Chowdhury, Kazi Kabiruddin (P. W.1), Mahbub Chowdhury and other elderly persons requested her husband to accept her. In her cross examination she denied the defence suggestion that the statements made above are not true and she had deposed falsely at the instance of P.W. I.

 

340. P. W.10 Shamsun Nahar, daughter of P.W.5 in her testimony stated that her maternal grand father and mother told that she is the daughter of Pakistani army and that Qaiser handed over her mother to Pakistani army, camped at Jagodishpur High School. Her mother gave birth of this witness after the war of Liberation. Freedom fighter Advocate Matin maintained this witness. She was given in marriage to one Afsar but when Afsar came to know that she is daughter of Pakistani army and he denied to accept this witness and, she was sent to her maternal grand father's house. In her cross examination, she denied the defence suggestion that the statements made above are not true.

 

341. Mr. S.M. Shahjahan, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that conviction awarded by the Tribunal solely on the basis of testimony of P.W.5 is illegal since she made vital contradictions in her evidence as to the involvement of the appellant in the occurrence.

 

342. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney General appearing for the respondents, submits that the offence charged against the appellant is very shocking and the victim herself stated in her evidence that a Qaiser himself handed her over to Pakistani army and members of Pak army raped her one after another keeping her confined in a room of Jogodishpur army camp along with other raped woman for about 8/10 days. There is nothing in evidence to disbelieve P.W.5.

 

343. From the testimony of P.W.5 it appears that she herself was the victim of the occurrence. She stated in her testimony,

 

‘কায়সার সাহেবের ভয়ে আমরা বিভিন্ন জায়গায় ফসলের ক্ষেতে পালিয়ে থাকতাম । বাংলা শ্রবান মাসের শেষের দিকে দুপুর বেলা আমার বাবা ও আইয়ুব আলী চাচাকে নিয়ে বাবার বাড়ীতে দুপুরের খাবার খেতে বসেছিলাম । এ সময়ে কায়সার বাহিনী ও রাজাকার বাহিনীর ১০-১২ জন সদস্য আমাদের বাড়ীতে ঢুকে আমার বাবাকে জিজ্ঞেস করলো মতিন (সাক্ষীর চাচা) কোথায়? কায়সার সাহেব বলেছে তাকে ধরে নিয়ে যেতে। আমার বাবা প্রত্যুত্তরে বললো মতিন কোথায় আমি তা জানিনা । এ সময় কায়সার বাহিনী ও রাজাকার বাহিনীর সদস্যরা আমার বাবাকে বন্দুক দিয়ে পিটাতে থাকে। বাবার চিৎকারে আমি ঘরের

 

ভিতরে থেকে চিৎকার দিয়ে কান্নাকাটি শুরু করি।তখন কায়সার বাহিনীর লোকেরা ভাতের থালা ও হাড়ি ফেলে দিয়ে আমার বাবা, আইয়ুব চাচা ও আমাকে ধরে নিয়ে জগদিশপুর হাইস্কুলে অবস্থিত পাকিস্তান আর্মি ক্যাম্পে নিয়ে যায়। সেখানে গিয়ে দেখি কায়সার সাহেব আছেন রাজাকার ও কায়সার বাহিনীর লোকেরা আমাকে ও আমার বাপ-চাচাকে কায়সারের সামনে হাজির করে। সেখানে আমি আরো দেখতে পাই ৭/৮ জন মেয়েকে আটক করে রেখে রাজাকার ও কায়সার বাহিনীর লোকেরা অস্ত্র হাতে পাহারা দিচ্ছে । এ সময় কায়সার সাহেব আমাকে পাকিস্তানী সেনাবাহিনীর হাতে তুলে দেয়। কায়সার সাহেব তখন আমার বাপ-চাচাকে জিজ্ঞেস করছিল মতিন কোথায়? আমার বাপ-চাচা মতিনের খবর দিতে না পারায় তাদেরকে ধাক্কা দিয়ে এক জায়গায় দাঁড় করিয়ে রাখে । তখন কায়সার সাহেব আমার বাপ-চাচাদেরকে দিয়ে একটি গর্ত খোড়ানোর জন্য রাজাকার ও তার বাহিনীর লোকদেরকে নির্দেশ দেয়। তখন আমার বাপ-চাচা এবং আরো ১০-১৫ জন লোকদের দিয়ে একটি বড় গর্ত খোঁড়ানো হয়। এ গর্তে দুই জন রাজাকারের প্রহরায় আমাকে রাখে । গর্ত খুড়তে খুড়তে আসরের নামাজের সময় হয়ে যায়। সন্ধ্যার দিয়ে আমার বাবা কায়সার সাহেবের কাছে আমাকে ছেড়ে দেওয়ার জন্য কাকুতি মিনতি করে। কিন্তু তিনি আমাকে ছাড়েনি । আমার বাবা কায়সার সাহেবকে

 

পূর্ব থেকেই চিনতেন। তখন আমার বাবা ও চাচাকে মৃত্যুর হুমকি দিয়ে ঐ ক্যাম্প থেকে তাড়িয়ে দেয়। সন্ধ্যার পর বৃষ্টি শুরু হলে রাজাকার ও কায়সার বাহিনীর সদস্যরা আমাকে গর্ত থেকে তুলে স্কুলের আর্মি ক্যাম্পের একটি কক্ষে ঢোকায়। সন্ধ্যার পর থেকে এ কক্ষে পাকিস্তান আর্মিরা আমার উপর পাবশিক নির্যাতন শুরু করে।

 

ক্যাম্পে আটক অন্য মহিলাদেরও চিৎকার শুনতে পাই। আমার উপর পাশবিক নির্যাতনের কারনে আমি চিৎকার করলে নির্যাতনকারী পাকিস্তান আর্মিরা আমার মুখে কাপড় গুজে দিত। সেই কক্ষে ৮-১০ দিন অনবরত পাকিস্তানী আর্মিরা আমার উপর পাশবিক নির্যাতন চালায় । এরই এক পর্যায়ে আমি অসুস্থ এবং অচল হয়ে পড়লে কায়সার সাহেব এসে আমার অবস্থা দেখে তার বাহিনীর সদস্য এবং রাজাকারদেরকে আমাকে

 

তুলে দিয়ে ফেলে দিতে বলে । আমার তখন কিছু জ্ঞান ছিল। আমি কায়সার সাহেবের কথাশুনতে পেয়েছি। রাজাকার এবং কায়সার বাহিনী সদস্যরা আমাকে কোথায় ফেলে আসবে জিজ্ঞেস করলে কায়সার সাহেব বলেছিল জগদিশপুর প্রাইমারী স্কুলের কাছে ফেলে দিতে । এরপর কায়সার বাহিনী ও রাজাকার বাহিনী সদস্যরা রাতের বেলায় আমাকে কাধে করে বয়ে নিয়ে সেখানে ফেলে দিয়ে আসে । এ সময় ঝাড়বৃষ্টি শুরু হয়। আমার সারা শরীরে রক্ত মাখা ছিল এবং পরনের কাপড় ছেড়া ছিল। ঝড় বাদলের কারনে সারা শরীরে কাদা লেগেছিল।সারারাত আমি খোলা আকাশের নিচে এভাবে পড়ে থাকি । আমার শরীরে পিঁপড়া পোকামাকড়

 

উঠেছিল আমি বুঝতে পারছিলাম। ভোরের দিকে হাটুর উপর ভর দিয়ে অনেক কষ্ট করে আধা মাইলের ও কম দুরত্বে আমার বাবার বাড়ীতে যাই।

 

344. This victim witness categorically stated that "Qaiser bahini" confining her, brought her to Jagodishpur army camp aiser himself handed her over to Pakistani army and members of Pak army repeatedly committed rape upon her keeping her confined for about 8/10 days in the army camp and, thereafter, at the instance of Qaiser she was thrown in the field of Jagadishpur primary school and, because of such recurrent rape the victim became pregnant and gave birth of P.W.10. We do not find any contradictions and discrepancies in the evidence of P.W.5. Upon perusal of the evidence of P.W.1, 5 and 10 and other circumstantial evidence, we do not find anything on record to disbelieve the testimonies of those P.Ws. It is relevant here to mention that abduction and rape of young women by the Pakistan army and their auxiliary forces in Bangladesh were common phenomenon during the war of liberation. In an interview Dr. Geoffrey Davis, obtained by one Bina Costa which was translated by Shilabrata Borman and published in the book “গণহত্যা” has given description of actual pictures in this regard committed in 1971, which is quoted below for reference,

 

“ড. জেফ্রি ডেভিস

 

যুদ্ধবিধবস্ত বাংলাদেশের স্বেচ্ছাসেবী একজন ডাক্তার

 

বীণা ডি কস্তা

 

আমি নারী মুক্তিযোদ্ধা, সমাজকর্মী, বীরাঙ্গনা প্রমুখের সাক্ষ্যৎকার গ্রহণ ও কাহিনী সংগ্রহ করার একপর্যায়ে নথিপত্রে ডঃ জেফরি ডেভিস নামে এক চিকিৎসকের উল্লেখ পাই, যিনি ১৯৭২ সালে যুদ্ধবিধ্বস্ত বাংলাদেশের কাজ করেছেন। নিম্নে তার সাক্ষাৎকারটি তুলে দেওয়া হলো। এই সাক্ষাৎকারের অংশ বিশেষ সিডনিতে তার বাড়িতে নেয়া এবং বাকিটা কাছাকাছি একটি রেস্তোরাঁয় বসে । এই সাক্ষাৎকারে। জাতি গঠনের কর্মকান্ডে সম্পৃক্ত নারী ও পুরুষের কাহিনীগুলো সংগ্রহনের প্রয়োজনীয়তা স্পষ্টভাবে ফুটে উঠেছে । আমাদের অনেকেই এখন সংকীর্ণ রাজনীতির বেড়াজালে আবদ্ধ হয়ে আছেন। আর এর ফলে ইতিহাস বিস্মৃতিতে আক্রান্ত হচ্ছে আমাদের জাতীয় বয়ান।

 

পাঠকদের মনে রাখা প্রয়োজন, আমার প্রশ্নের উত্তর খুঁজতে গিয়ে ড. ডেভিস প্রায় ৩২ বছর আগেরকার ঘটনাবলি স্মরন করার চেষ্টা করছিলেন। এ কারণে কয়েক স্থানে তার জবাব অস্পষ্ট মনে হতে পারে। সিডনি, এন স ডবু, অষ্টেলিয়ার এক মেডিকেল গ্রাজুয়েট ড. জেফ্রি ডেভিস ১৯৭২ সালের মার্চ থেকে প্রায় ছয় মাস বাংলাদেশে কাজ করেছেন। তিনি ইন্টারন্যশনাল প-্যানড প্যারেন্টহুড, ইউএনএফপিএ এবং ডব্লিও এইচ ও এর পৃষ্ঠপোষকতায় কাজ করেছেন। স্মৃতিচারনার শুরুতেই তিনি জানান, তার কাজের অত্যান্ত স্পর্শকাতর প্রকৃতির কারনে কোন সংগঠনই তাকে তাদের লোক হিসাবে দাবী করতে রাজি ছিল না।

 

ড. ডেভিস স্মৃতিচারণ করতে গিয়ে বলেন, পশ্চিম পাকিস্তানি সৈন্যরা তাদের ক্যাম্পে বাঙ্গালি মেয়েদের বন্দি করে রাখার সময় জন্মানো যেসব শিশু বেঁচে গেছে, তাদেরকে টিকিয়ে রাখার চেষ্টা করছিলাম আমরা । এছাড়া আমাদের ওপর নির্দেশ ছিল, যে সমস্ত নারীর ভ্রুণ জন্মগ্রহণের জন্য তৈরী হয় নাই তাদের গর্ভপাত ঘটানোর চেষ্টা করা যাতে তাদেরকে রোগাক্রান্ত ও পুষ্টিহীন শিশুর জন্ম দিতে না হয়। আর এ কাজে আমরা সফল হয়েছি । এটা ঠিক যে, নির্যাতিত মেয়ের সংখ্যা ছিল বিপুল। তবে আমরা সেখানে পৌছানোর আগেই অনেক মহিলাকে মেরে ফেলা হয়েছিল । অথবা অনেকেই তাদের পরিবারে ফেরত পাঠানো হয়েছিল। পরিস্থিতি ছিল আতঙ্কজনক। আমরা বুঝলাম, আমাদের বসে থাকলে চলবে না। কী করা যায় সেটা ভেবে বের করার চেষ্টা করছিলাম । সেসময় ইংল্যান্ড থেকেও আরেকজন এসেছিলেন । কিন্ত পরে আমি তার খোঁজ হারিয়ে ফেলি। পরিস্থিতিটা সত্যি বীভৎস ছিল।

 

প্রশ্নঃ আপনি কি স্বেচ্ছাপ্রণোদিত হয়ে সেখানে গিয়েছিলেন?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা, স্বেচ্ছাপ্রণোদিত হয়েই গেছি।

 

প্রশ্নঃ এই কাজ করার ইচ্ছে আপনার কেন হয়েছিল?

 

জেফ্রিঃ এডভাল প্রেগনেন্সি টার্মিনেট করার কৌশল জানা ছিল আমার । আমি মূলত ইংল্যান্ড থেকে ট্রেনিং নিয়েছি। যাহোক আমি সাধারনত ৩০ সপ্তাহের নিচের প্রেগনেন্সি টার্মিনেট করছিলাম।

 

প্রশ্নঃ  ঢাকায় কোথায় কাজ করেছেন আপনি?

 

জেফ্রিঃ আমি ধানমন্ডির একটি ক্লিনিকে কাজ করেছি। অন্যান্য শহরে হাসপাতালের যেসব ধ্বংসাবশেষ ছিল, সেগুলোতেও আমি কাজ করেছি। আমি মূলত যা করেছিলাম সংখ্যা এতো বিপুল ছিল -- সেসব শহরের লোকজনকে প্রশিক্ষণ দিতে শুরু করি। তারা কিছুটা রপ্ত করে ফেলতেই আমি পরের শহরের দিকে পা বাড়াই ।

 

প্রশ্ন : রেকর্ডের স্বার্থে আপনি দয়া করে বলবেন কি, সেখানে আপনি ঠিক কী কাজ করছিলেন?

 

জেফ্রিঃ আমি যাওয়ার সামান্য আগে সেখানে একটি নারী পূণর্বাসন সংগঠন তৈরী করা হয়। সেটির দায়িত্বে ছিলেন বিচারপতি কে,এম, সোবহান। তারা গর্ভবতী সকল মহিলাকে এক জায়গায় নিরাপদে রাখার চেষ্টা করছিলেন এবং ব্যবস্থা করছিলেন। আর যারা সন্তানের জন্ম দিয়েছে তাদের সন্তানদের সংগ্রহ করে আমরা ইন্টারন্যাশনাল সোশ্যাল সার্ভিসের (আইএসএস) হাতে তুলে দিচ্ছিলাম -----।

 

প্রশ্নঃ সেসময় আপনার সঙ্গে আর কারা কাজ করেছিল মনে করতে পারেন কি?

 

জেফ্রিঃ যুদ্ধোত্তর পুনবার্সন কেন্দ্রের প্রধান ছিলেন বিচারপতি সোবহান। আর মুল সক্রিয় ব্যক্তিটি ছিলেন ভন সচুক—তিনি ছিলেন সুইডিশ। তার নামের প্রথম অংশটি মনে করতে পারছি না। আমার মনে হয়, তার স্ত্রীর নাম ছিল মেরি। তারা অর্থ দিয়ে সাহায্য করেছিলেন । বাঙ্গালী কর্মকর্তাদের নাম আমি মনে করতে পারছি না ---- | তাছাড়া কেউ তো এই ইতিহাস জানতে কখনও আগ্রহ প্রকাশ করেনি--- ।"

 

জেফ্রিঃ এ কথা কেন মনে হয়েছে আপনার?

 

জেফ্রিঃ এর কারণ এর সঙ্গে গর্ভপাত এবং সন্তান দত্তক নেয়ার বিষয় জড়িত ছিল । আরেকটা ব্যাপার হলো, পশ্চিম পাকিস্তান একটা কমনওয়েলথভুক্ত দেশ। আর এর কর্মকর্তাদের সকলেই ব্রিটেনে প্রশিক্ষণপ্রাপ্ত ৷ এটা বৃটিশ সরকারের কাছে ছিল অত্যান্ত বিব্রতকর একটা ব্যাপার । পশ্চিম পাকিস্তানি কর্মকর্তারা বুঝতে পারছিল না এ নিয়ে এতো হৈচৈ করা হচ্ছে কেন। আমি তাদের অনেকের সঙ্গে কথা বলেছি। তারা কুমিল্লার একটি কারাগারে বন্দি ছিল। খুব করুণ অবস্থায় ছিল তারা (হাসি--- যেটি তাদের প্রাপ্য ছিল)। আর তারা বলেছিল, এরা কী করতে চাচ্ছে ? আমাদের কী করা উচিৎ ছিল বলে এরা মনে করে? এটা তো যুদ্ধ রে ভাই।

 

প্রশ্নঃ তারা নারী ধর্ষণের ব্যাপারটা কীভাবে জায়েজ করার চেষ্টা করেছে?

 

জেফ্রিঃ ওরে বাপস! তাদের ওপর টিক্কা খানের এক প্রকার আদেশ বা নির্দেশই ছিল যে, একজন সাচ্চা মুসলমান তার বাবা ছাড়া সবারই সঙ্গেই লড়াই করবে। কাজেই তাদের যা করতে হবে তা হলো যতোটা পারা যায়। বেশিসংখ্যাক বাঙ্গালী নারীকে গর্ভবতী করা । এটাই ছিল তাদের কাজের পেছনের তত্ত্ব ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ মেয়েদের গর্ভবতী করতে হবে কেন? এর কারণটা কি আপনাকে তারা বলেছে?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা, বলেছে, (তারা বলেছে)। এর ফলে পূর্ব পাকিস্তানে এমন একটা গোটা প্রজন্ম সৃষ্টি হবে, যাদের শরীরে বইবে পশ্চিম পাকিস্তানিদের রক্ত তারা একথাটাইবলেছে।

 

প্রশ্ন : পাকিস্তানিদের অসংখ্য নথিপত্রে এখনও বলা হয়, ধর্ষণের ঘটনার সংখ্যা অত্যান্ত বাড়িয়ে বলা হচ্ছে আপনি কি তাদের এ দাবি সত্য মনেকরেন?

 

জেফ্রিঃ না, না, --- তারা ধর্ষণ করেছে। সম্ভবত তারা প্রকৃতই যা করেছে , তার তুলনায় অনেকগুণ কমসংখ্যা দাবি করা হয়। তারা যে পদ্ধতিতে শহর দখল করতে তার বিবরণ খুব কৌতুহলোদ্দীপক। তারা তাদের পদাতিক বাহিনীকে পেছনে রেখে গোলন্দাজ বাহিনীকে সামনে নিয়ে আসতো। তারপর হাসপাতাল, স্কুল-কলেজ গোলা ছুঁড়ে গুঁড়িয়ে দিতো। এর ফলে শহরে নেমে আসততা চরম বিশৃংখলা । আর তারপর পদাতিক বাহিনী শহরে ঢুকে পড়ে মেয়েদের বেছে বেছে আলাদা করতো । শিশুরা ছাড়া যৌনভাবে ম্যাচিওরড সকল মেয়েকে তারা একত্রে জড়ো করতো । আর শহরের বাকি লোকজনকে বন্দি করে ফেলতো পদাতিক বাহিনীর অন্যারা। আওয়ামী লীগের সঙ্গ যুক্ত সবাইকে গুলি করে মেরে ফেলা হতো । আর তারপর মেয়েদের পাহাড়া দিতে কম্পাউন্ডে নিয়ে এসে সৈন্যদের মাঝে বিলিয়ে দেয়া হতো। অত্যা��্ত জঘন্য একটা ব্যাপার ছিল এটা । বিশ্বের কোথাও কখনও এমন ঘটনার নজির পাওযা যায় না। তবুও এমনটাই ঘটেছিল।

 

প্রশ্নঃ যুদ্ধের অভিজ্ঞতা নিয়ে ক্লিনিকের নারী-পুরুষ বা কোনো সমাজকর্মীদের ও সঙ্গে কোনোকথা হয়েছে আপনার? বিশেষত ধর্ষণ শিবিরের (রেপ ক্যাম্প) মেয়েদের অভিজ্ঞতার ব্যাপারে?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা, আমরা সব সময় এসব অভিজ্ঞতার কথা শুনতাম । তারা যেসব ঘটনার কথা বলতো তার কোন কোনটা ছিল রীতিমত রক্ত হিম করা। বিশালদেহী পাকিস্তানী সৈন্যদের দ্বারা বারবার ধর্ষিত হওয়ার কাহিনী শুনেছি আমরা। আপনি বিশ্বাস করতে পারবেন না, কেউ এ ধরনের কাজ করতে পারে। ধনী এবং সুন্দরী মেয়েদেরকে অফিসারদের জন্য রেখে দেয়া হতো আর বাকিদের অন্যান্য রাঙ্কের সৈন্যদের মধ্যে বন্টন করে দেয়া হতো। আর মেয়েদের দারুণ কষ্টে ফেলে দেয়া হতো । তাদেরকে পর্যাপ্ত খেতে দেয়া হতো না। অসুস্থ হয়ে পড়লে তাদের চিকিৎসা দেয়া হতো না! অনেকেই ক্যাম্পের মধ্যে মারা গেছে। এসব ঘটনা সহজে কেউ বিশ্বাস করছিল না। এগুলো যে সত্যি ঘটতে পারে, এটা বিশ্বাস করতে কেউ রাজি ছিল না। কিন্তু এ সংক্রান্ত তথ্যগুলোই প্রমাণ করছে। যে, ঘটনাগুলো সত্যি।

 

প্রশ্ন: হ্যাঁ, আপনার কথা আমি বুঝতে পারছি। আপনি জানেন গত চার বছর ধরে আমি নিজেও এসব মেয়েকে খুঁজে বের করার চেষ্টা করছি। তারা সংখ্যায় বিপুল। তাদের অনেককেই পাওয়া যাওয়ার কথা কিন্ত আমি নিজে খুবই কমসংখ্যক মেয়েকে খুঁজে পেয়েছি।

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা, অনেকেই অস্বীকার করেছে। তারা ব্যাপারটা একেবারে চেপে গেছে। এমনটা হয়।

 

প্রশ্নঃ যুদ্ধের পরপরই পরিস্থিতি কি কিছুটা ভিন্নতর ছিল? কেউ কি তার অভিজ্ঞতা জানিয়েছে?

 

জেফ্রিঃ কেউ এ বিষয়ে কথা বলতে রাজি ছিল না। আপনি প্রশ্নের পর প্রশ্ন করে যাবেন, কিন্তু কোনো উত্তর পাবেন না। মাঝে মাঝে এমনও হয়েছে, তারা স্মৃতি হারিয়ে ফেলেছে। পুরুষরাও কেউ এ বিষয়ে একদম কথা বলতে রাজি ছিল না। কেননা তাদের মতে, মেয়েরা কলঙ্কিত হয়ে গেছে। আর বাংলাদেশে মেয়েদের মর্যাদা অনেক কম, এটাও ঠিক। এরকম অবস্থায় তারা সম্ভ্রম হারালে তাদের কোনো মর্যাদাই আর অবশিষ্ট থাকে না । তাদের তখন বাঁচা মরার কোনো তফাত থাকে না। আর পুরুষরা তাদের মেরে ফেলেছে। আমি বিশ্বাস করতে পারছিলাম না। পশ্চিমা বিশ্বে এমনটা কল্পনাই করা যায়।

 

প্রশ্নঃ আপনি নিশ্চয় বাংলা বলতে পারতেন না। আপনার পক্ষে মানুষের সঙ্গে কথা বলতে কি বেগ পেতে হতো?

 

জেফ্রিঃ না। আমার একজন দোভাষী ছিলেন। একজন পুরুষ দোভাষী । তারা সবাই খুব দ্রুত সংগঠিত হয়ে গিয়েছিল। তারা আমাকে একটা ল্যান্ডরোভার যোগাড় করে দিল। একজন ড্রাইভার আর একজন ফিল্ড অফিসার পেয়েছিলাম আমি। ওই ফিল্ড অফিসার আমার দোভাষীর কাজ করে দিতেন। ড্রাইভারের নাম ছিল মমতাজ । তবে ফিল্ড অফিসারের নাম মনে করতে পারছি না। তিনি একজন সরকারী চাকুরে ছিলেন। সরকারি কর্মকর্তাদের অধিকাংশই ইংরেজীতে কথা বলতে পারতেন। তিউনিশিয়ায় যে কষ্ট করতে হয়েছে,

 

এখানে সেটা হয়নি (ড. ডেভিস তিউনিশিয়ায় জনসংখ্যা কার্যক্রমের কাজ করেছেন)।

 

প্রশ্নঃ মেয়েরা কেন এ ব্যাপারে নীরব ছিল, আপনার কী মনে হয়?

 

জেফ্রিঃ আতঙ্কে । তারা সবাই দুঃস্বপ্ন দেখতো । সেই আতংক কখনোই কাটিয়ে ওঠা যায়। অধিকাংশেরই ভীষন স্নায়বিক উদ্বেগ দেখা দেয়। আর তাছাড়া আমরা ছিলাম বিদেশি । তারা কোনো বিদেশিকে বিশ্বাস করতে পারছিল না। তাদেরকে নিয়ে আমরা কী করতে যাচ্ছি তারা জানতো না—

 

প্রশ্নঃ ধর্ষণ শিবিরগুলো যেখানে ছিল, সেরকম কোনো জায়গায় কি আপনি গেছেন?

 

জেফ্রিঃ ধর্ষণ শিবিরগুলো ততোদিনে তুলে দেয়া হয়েছিল এবং পুণর্বাসন সংগঠন সেখান থেকে মেয়েদেরকে তাদের নিজ নিজ গ্রাম ও শহরে পাঠিয়ে দেয়ার চেষ্টা করছিল। তবে অনেক ক্ষেত্রে যেটা ঘটেছে যে, স্ত্রীকে স্বামীর কাছে ফেরত পাঠানোর পর স্বামী স্ত্রীকে মেরে ফেলে। কেননা স্ত্রী তার সম্ভম হারিয়েছে। অনেক ক্ষেত্রে কী

 

ঘটেছে জানারও চেষ্টা করতো না তারা। দেশের প্রত্যন্ত অঞ্চলে, যমুনা নদীতে লাশ ভাসতে দেখা গেছে। এ ঘটনাটি ইউরোপে উদ্বেগ সৃষ্টি করেছিল । কিন্তু এগুলো অব্যাহত ছিল।

 

প্রশ্নঃ যে সব মেয়েরা কথা কি আপনার মনে আছে? কতোজনের গর্ভপাত ঘটিয়াছেন আপনি?

 

জেফ্রিঃ সঠিক পরিসংখ্যান স্মরন করা কঠিন। তবে দিনে প্রায় একশ জন করে।

 

প্রশ্নঃ ঢাকায়, না দেশের অন্যান্য অংশে?

 

জেফ্রিঃ সংখ্যা উল্লেখ করা কঠিন। ঢাকায় গড়ে দিনে একশ জন করে, আর দেশের অন্যত্র সংখাটা ওঠানামা করেছে। কেউ কেউ কলকাতায় গিয়েছিল---

 

প্রশ্ন : শতকরা হারে বলতে পারবেন? যেমন ধরুণ শ্রেনীভিত্তিক, ধর্মভিত্তিক দিক থেকে কতজন মেয়ের দেখা পেয়েছেন।

 

জেফ্রিঃ সব শ্রেনীর মেয়েই ছিল। তাদের ধর্ম নিয়ে আমাদের মাথাব্যাথ্যা ছিল না---আমরা শুধু তাদের বিপদ থেকে উদ্ধার করার চেষ্টা করেছি। তবে মোটের ওপর বলা যায়, যারা ধনী তারা যুদ্ধের পরপরই কলকাতা চলে গিয়ে গর্ভপাত ঘটাতে পেরেছিল ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ গর্ভপাত ঘটাতে রাজি কিনা মেয়েদের কাছে সেটা কি জানতে চাওয়া হতো? তাদের ইচ্ছা.... অনিচ্ছার ব্যাপার ছিল কি?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হাঁ, অবশ্যই । আমার যতোজন মেয়ে পেয়েছিলাম তাদের সবাই গর্ভপাত ঘটাতে চেয়েছিল । এতে রাজি নয়। এমন কাউকে আমরা পাইনি। অন্যদিকে যেসব মেয়ে সন্তানের জন্ম দিয়েছিল, তারা তাদের সন্তানকে পুণর্বাসন সংগঠনের হাতে তুলে দিয়েছিল। আর এভাবে এসব শিশু আইএসএসের কাছে এবং অন্যান্য দেশে পৌছেছে । তবে তারা সংখ্যায় কতো আমার কোনো ধারনা নেই।

 

প্রশ্নঃ এ ব্যাপারে বিশদ প্রশ্ন করায় আমি আপনার কাছে ক্ষমা চেয়ে নিচ্ছি। তবে পুর্ণবাসন কর্মকান্ডে তাদের মতামত বা ইচ্ছা-অনিচ্ছার সুযোগ রাখা হয়েছিল কিনা এ ব্যাপারে আমার সত্যিকার কৌতুহল রয়েছে। গর্ভপাত ঘটানোর সময় কোনো মহিলা কাঁদছিল বা মানসিকভাবে ভেঙ্গে পড়েছিল এমন কোনো ঘটনা কি মনে করতে পারেন?

 

জেফ্রিঃ না তাদের কেউই কাঁদেনী। তারা খুবই শক্তমনের পরিচয় দিয়েছিল। তারা একেবারেই কান্নাকাটি করেনি। তারা একেবারে শান্ত থেকেছে। ও, ঈশ্বরকে ধণ্যবাদ। এর ফলে আমাদের পক্ষে ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ আপনি বলেছেন, যেসব মহিলা গর্ভপাত ঘটাতে রাজি ছিলেন, আপনি শুধু তাদেরই চিকিৎসা দিয়েছেন । আমি আমার সে প্রসঙ্গে ফিরে যেতে চাই । মহিলারা তাদের সম্মতি কাকে জানিয়েছিল? সংশ্লিষ্ট ডাক্তারদের, নার্সদের, সমাজ-কর্মীদের?

 

জেফ্রিঃ ও হ্যাঁ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ তাদের কি কোনো কাগজে স্বাক্ষর করতে হয়েছে?

 

জেফ্রিঃ আমার মনে হয় তাদেরকে সম্মতিসূচক একটা ডকুমেন্ট স্বাক্ষর করতে হয়েছিল। তবে আমি নিশ্চিত নই। সরকার পরোক্ষভাবে ব্যাপারটা আয়োজন করেছিল। এটার আয়োজন মুলত করেছিল পুণর্বাসন সংগঠন এবং আর যেসব মহিলা তাদের সাহায্য করেছিল তারা । তবে এটা নিশ্চিত যে, যারা গর্ভপাত ঘটাতে রাজি ছিল না, তারা কেউ ক্লিনিকের কাছে ঘেঁষেনি। কাজেই এটা কোনো ইস্যু ছিল না।

 

প্রশ্নঃ আপনি কি শেষ পর্যন্ত গর্ভপাত ঘটিয়েছেন? সেটা তো গর্ভধারণের একটা অগ্রসর পর্যায় হওয়ার কথা, তাই না?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা, সেখানে আমার ছয় মাসের অবস্থানকালে পুরো সময়টাই আমি গর্ভপাত ঘটিয়েছি। মহিলারা এমন তীব্র অপুষ্টিতে ভুগছিল যে, ৪০ সপ্তাহের ভ্রণ প্রায় ১৮ সপ্তাহের একটি ভ্রুনের সমান হতো ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ নারীদের কোনরকম পরামর্শ দেয়া হতো কিনা মনে করতে পারেন?

 

জেফ্রিঃ পরামর্শ? পুণর্বাসন সংগঠন তা দিতো । সেখানে নারী সমাজকর্মীরা তাদের সঙ্গে কথা বলতেন। আমার মনে হয় না তাতে তাদের খুব একটা লাভ হতো। কেননা তারা সবাই ছিল অপুষ্টিতে ভোগা । যৌনরোগ ও অপুষ্টিজনিত রোগবালাইয়ে আক্রান্ত ছিল তারা। খুব ভয়ঙ্কর পরিস্থিতি ছিল সেটা । দেশে তখন এসব সমস্যা মোকাবিলার মতো সম্পদ, ওষধপত্র বা সুযোগ সুবিধা একেবারেই ছিল না। সীমিত সম্পদ যাছিল তাও যুদ্ধাহত সেন্যদের জন্য রাখা ছিল । মেয়েদের জন্য কিছুই অবশিষ্ট ছিল না। আমাদের নিজেদের ষ্টাফ নিয়ে আসতে হয়েছিল ।

 

জেফ্রিঃ আপনারা সরবরাহ কোথা থেকে পেতেন? সেগুলো কি যথেষ্ট ছিল?

 

জেফ্রিঃ ইংল্যান্ড থেকে । আমাকে আমার নিজের প্রয়োজনীয় জিনিসপত্র নিয়ে আসতে বলা হয়েছিল। এছাড়া আমি দুই সেট যন্ত্রপাতি ও এন্টিবায়েটিক সঙ্গে নিয়েছিলাম ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ ছয়মাস ধরে গর্ভপাত ঘটানোর কাজে আপনি মাত্র দুই সেট যন্ত্রপাতি ব্যবহার করেছিলেন?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা । স্থানীয় হাসপাতালের যন্ত্রপাতিগুলো সব ধবংস করে ফেলা হয়েছিল। ওষুধপত্র যা অবশিষ্ট ছিল, তার সবই ছিল যুদ্ধাহতদের জন্য ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ সেই যন্ত্রপাতিগুলোকি শারীরিকভাবে নিরাপদ ছিল?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যাঁ, বিশেষজ্ঞ অল্প বয়সীদের ক্ষেত্রে সেসব রোগবালাই শরীরে নিয়ে সন্তান জন্ম দেয়ার চেয়ে এটাই বরং নিরাপদ ছিল ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ আপনি কি গর্ভপাত ও দত্তক গ্রহণ উভয় কর্মকান্ডের সঙ্গেই যুক্ত ছিলেন?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা। তবে দত্তক কর্মসূচীর ক্ষেত্রে শুধু শিশুদের আইএসএসের হাতে তুলে দেয়া আমার কাজ ছিল। গর্ভপাত ঘটানো ও জন্ম নেওয়া শিশুর সংখ্যা ছিল বিপুল । যুদ্ধের সময় মেয়েদের যেসব সামরিক কম্পাউন্ডে রাখা হয়েছিল, সেগুলোর আকার নিশ্চয়ই বিশাল ছিল । তবে আমি সেখানে যাওয়ার আগেই সেগুলো বন্ধ করে দেয়া হয়েছিল।

 

প্রশ্নঃ ঢাকা শহরের বাইরে যেসব জায়গায় আপনি গেছেন সেগুলোর অবস্থা কেমন ছিল? সেখানে কী ধরণের সুযোগ সুবিধা আপনারা পেয়েছেন ।

 

জেফ্রিঃ হাসপাতাল আর পুনর্বাসন সংগঠন ---সেটার নাম কী ছিল, আমি মনে করতে পারছি না। সম্ভবত বাংলাদেশ জাতীয় নারী পুনর্বাসন সংগঠন বা এ জাতীয় কিছু । বেশির ভাগ বড় কেন্দ্রগুলোর এরাই কাজ করছিল। আমার যাওয়ার আগে সেখানে খুব অল্পসংখ্যাক গর্ভপাত করা হয়েছিল। কেননা কেউ সেটা করতে চাচ্ছিল না। হাসপাতালের মেডিক্যাল স্টাফদের বেশির ভাগ মনে করছিল এটা বে-আইনী কাজ । যা, হোক, আমার কাজ অনুমোদন করে আমি স্বরাষ্ট্র সচিব রব চৌধুরীর কাছ থেকে একটি চিঠি পেয়েছিলাম।

 

সেখানে বলা হয়েছিল, আমি যা করতে চাচ্ছি, তা আইনসিদ্ধ এবং তারা সবরকম সাহায্য দিতে রাজি আছেন । চিঠিটা আমি এখন আর খুঁজে বের করতে পারবো না। এটা সম্ভবত এখানেই কোথাও আছে---বাংলাদেশ সংক্রান্ত প্রচুর কাগজপত্র জমিয়ে রেখেছি আমি---- এগুলোকে আমার গুরুত্বপূর্ণ মনে হয়েছে, বাংলাদেশে যা দেখেছি তেমনটা পৃথিবীর আর কোথাও ঘটতে দেখবো না আমি । কাজেই আমি এসব কাগজপত্র রেখে দিয়েছি । সেসময় এগুলো খুবই ভয়ঙ্কর মনে হচ্ছিল।

 

প্রশ্নঃ মেয়েদের সবাই কি গর্ভপাত করাতে বা সন্তানকে দত্তক দিতে রাজি হয়েছে? কেউ কি সন্তানকে রেখে দিতে চায়নি?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা --- দুয়েকজন চেয়েছে---

 

প্রশ্নঃ আপনি কি জানেন তাদের ভাগ্যে কী ঘটেছিল?

 

জেফ্রিঃ আমার কোন ধারনা নেই। আইএসএস সেখানে যতো শিশু পারা যায় সংগ্রহ করেছে। কেননা আমেরিকা ও পশ্চিম ইউরোপে তখন দত্তক নেয়ার মতো শিশুর অভাব দেখা দিয়েছিল। আর তারা যতোটা পারা যায় বেশিসংখ্যক শিশু সংগ্রহ করার চেষ্টা করছিল।

 

প্রশ্নঃ ইন্টারন্যাশনাল সোশ্যাল সার্ভিসেস?

 

জেফ্রিঃ হ্যা। সংস্থাটি ওয়াশিংটন ডিসি ভিত্তিক। দত্তক সংক্রান্ত প্রথম সারির সংস্থা ।

 

প্রশ্নঃ মায়েদেরে কী হতো?

 

জেফ্রিঃ গর্ভপাত বা সন্তান জন্ম দেওয়ার পর তারা কিছুদিন সেখানে থাকতো আর তারপর ত্রান পুনর্বাসন কেন্দ্রে গিয়ে আশ্রয় নিতো। তারা যতোদিন খুশি সেখানে থাকতে পারতো । তারপর তারা নানারকম প্রশিক্ষণ কর্মসূচীতে যোগ দিতো। আমি তাদের দু'য়েক জন দেখেছি। বাণিজ্যিক ভিত্তিক পোশাক তৈরী করছিল তারা। ঢাকা, দিনাজপুর, রংপুর নোয়াখালীতে এমনটা দেখেছি। সাক্ষাতকার দেওয়ার জন্য ড. ডেভিসকে আমার আন্তরিক ধন্যবাদ। তাঁর কাছ থেকে বিদায় নেয়ার আগে আমরা আরেকবার তাঁর বাংলাদেশ সফরের ব্যাপারে বিস্তারিত আলোচনা করেছি। আমাদের যুদ্ধাপরাধ টাইব্যুনাল গঠনের সম্ভাব্যতার প্রসঙ্গে এসে পড়ে । জেফ্রি আমার হাত শক্ত করে ধরে সেটি তার বুকে রাখেন। তাঁর চোখে অশ্রু। বাংলাদেশ ন্যায় বিচার পাওয়ার চেষ্টা করলে তিনি তার সাধ্যে সবকিছু করবেন বলে জানান। প্রাথমিক পদক্ষেপ হিসেবে আমি সত্যি আশা করি, এই সাক্ষাৎকার আগ্রহী গ্রুপকে তার কাহিনী আনুষ্ঠানিকভাবে লিপিবদ্ধ করতে উৎসাহিত:

 

করবে।”

 

345. It is also relevant here to narrate another identical occurrence committed by Pakistan army on our mother land in 1971 which are as follows:

 

346. In M. Akhtaruzzaman Mondol's "Amader-Ma Bon" translated by Sohela Nazneen it was, inter alia, stated:
